question: In Five year plans, Plan Holiday is from ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**1966-1969.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Plan Holiday:-**

 
 
• It​ was a **break** in the **Five Year Plans of India**, during which** no new plan** was launched.
 
• It was from** 1966 to 1969** when the **third plan ended** and the** fourth plan began.**
 
• The break was taken to evaluate the** progress** of the previous plans and to make **necessary changes **in the upcoming plan.
 
• The decision to take a Plan Holiday was made by the then** Prime Minister of India, Indira Gandhi.**
 
• The Plan Holiday helped in** improving the economy** and **reducing poverty **in India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Five-Year Plans:-**

 
 
• **It refer to the country's series of comprehensive economic development strategies. **
 
• The planning process was initiated by the Planning Commission (and later replaced by NITI Aayog).
 
• Each plan outlined the government's priorities, sectoral allocations, and development goals for a five-year period.
 
• The concept of five-year plans was popularized by the Soviet Union under Joseph Stalin's leadership. The Soviets used these plans to rapidly industrialize and develop the economy.
